newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares beat steep retreat by close.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares beat steep retreat by close.

text.p: Italian stocks tumbled by the close on Thursday as selling set in first on futures and then in cash after Wall Street and bonds slid following a rise in part of the July Chicago Purchasing Managers Index.
"Someone started selling on the futures and then it spread to the cash market," a broker here said, adding he saw no reason domestically for the fall.
"It feels like people had their fingers on the button ready to sell. They're lightening their luggage and selling before they go off on holiday," the broker added.
Volume shortly before the close was around 1.4 trillion lire ($779 million).
The blue-chip Mib30 index ended 1.14 percent down at 22,256 while the all-share Mibtel was 0.75 percent off at 14,694. On the futures, the Sept contract was 1.45 percent down at 22,480.
"The fall in New York and on the Btp futures convinced the market to go for a decisive drop," another broker said.

On individual stocks, information technology group Olivetti, which has fallen sharply recently, had a slight rebound as the company held a board meeting and was expected to release some first half figures. Olivetti ended 4.47 percent up at 674 lire.

The group said after the market closed its revenues for the first half of 1997 were down 10.4 percent on the first six months of 1996 and that Rodolfo De Benedetti, son of former chairman Carlo De Benedetti, had resigned from the board.
Italian bank Ambroveneto was up 3.49 percent at 10,205 lire after signing its merger accord with Cariplo.
Other bluechips like carmaker Fiat and energy group ENI were both weak, with Fiat off 1.91 percent at 5,953 lire and ENI buckling 0.71 percent to 10,558 lire.
